title: Create a CSV list of files in a folder
summary: Scan subfolders and record file paths, extensions, sizes, and modification times in a table. Start with 4 small example files while keeping the originals and existing results intact.
audience: Python beginners who have been manually listing the number and locations of documents in a folder
prerequisites: Install Python 3.12 or later and check the version in a terminal with python --version.
Extract the example ZIP into a new folder. Do not run the example from inside the ZIP archive.
Open a terminal in the folder containing example.py. If the python command is unavailable on Windows, use py. On macOS or Linux, use python3 if your environment requires it.
No external packages or accounts are needed. The included files are synthetic data created for this tutorial.

sections.heading: Create your first list with four files

blocks.text: Creating an output folder is not enough to call this task complete. The CSV must contain each of the four original files exactly once, the listed sizes must total 63 bytes, and the original contents must remain unchanged. Check these conditions with the included data before moving on to your own work folder.

items: Find example.py, README.txt, and the sample_files folder in the extracted folder.
Open sample_files and check readme.txt, empty.txt, and the docs and reports subfolders. empty.txt is intentionally empty.
Run the command below once in the terminal. Do not move or edit the input files while it runs.
When the completion message and output path appear, open outputs/file_list.csv.

blocks.title: Please check
blocks.text: This example does not read or analyze file contents. It checks paths, sizes, and modification times, so no additional libraries for specific document formats are needed.

The code starts from the location of example.py, not the current terminal folder. It scans only sample_files under BASE, so you can move the whole example folder as long as its internal layout stays the same. outputs sits outside the scanned folder so the result CSV does not enter the input list on a later run.

rows: Files with the same name are distinguishable if they are in different folders.
No extension is shown as (없음); tar.gz is shown as .gz.
File size as an integer number of bytes
0 means an empty file, not a missing value.
The trailing +00:00 means UTC, which differs from Korean local time.

blocks.text: relative_path uses forward slashes for readability across operating systems. Results are sorted by this path. They do not depend on the internal file traversal order, making it easier to compare row order for the same input.

sections.heading: Full code used in this example

blocks.text: collect_files gathers file information, and main writes a new CSV. The code does not create outputs until input checks are complete. If it encounters an unreadable folder or a link, it stops rather than saving a partial list as a successful result.

csv.DictWriter handles CSV delimiters and quoting. The file is saved with newline set to an empty string and a UTF-8 BOM. The output file is opened in x mode so it will not overwrite a file that already exists. This example first checks whether the outputs folder itself exists.

sections.heading: Check the four rows and total size

blocks.text: The table totals 15 + 0 + 17 + 31 = 63 bytes. The terminal also displays “완료: 4개 파일, 합계 63바이트” (complete: four files, sixty-three bytes total). The first line of the CSV contains column names, so a spreadsheet shows five rows including the header. Do not forget to count empty.txt.

blocks.title: Please check
blocks.text: modified_utc values may differ depending on where you extract or copy the files. Compare paths and sizes when checking the example results; the date strings do not have to match.

sections.heading: Check the originals as well as the list

items: Match each of the four paths in the CSV to its actual location in sample_files. The docs and reports folders themselves are not included as data rows.
Check that the empty file is included with a size of 0 bytes and that the extensions are .txt and .csv.
Open sample_files/readme.txt and check that the original text Sample inventory is still there.
Run the same command again. It should stop with “outputs가 이미 있습니다” (outputs already exists), and the first result should remain intact.

blocks.text: Failure conditions are part of the design. Do not remove the output-protection code just because it blocks a repeated run. To keep the previous results, rename outputs to a name containing a date before running again, or extract the ZIP into a new folder to start a new test.

sections.heading: Apply it to your own folder

blocks.text: Do not point the example at your entire work folder at first. Put a few representative files in a copy of sample_files. Path objects handle filenames containing Korean characters or spaces. Symbolic links and directory junctions that point elsewhere are outside the supported scope, so use a small copy containing regular files.

items: Keep the existing example inputs and results, and create a new practice folder.
Place 5~10 files in sample_files so you can count them by hand. Include one level of subfolders as well.
Generate the list and check that the relative paths point to the expected locations.
Increase the number of files while keeping the checked rules unchanged. File size can differ from content length, so keep the unit as bytes.

blocks.text: If the input folder is empty, the script creates a header-only CSV and reports a file count of 0. This differs from stopping because the folder is missing. An empty folder can be a valid work state, so distinguish the two when interpreting results.

rows: A problem with the Python launcher installation or path settings
Check python --version first, and try py on Windows.
sample_files must be a real folder
The folder is missing or a link is being used
Check that you extracted the entire ZIP and restore a real folder.
Results from a previous run are still present
Move the existing results somewhere safe, then run again.
The program opening the file is interpreting its encoding incorrectly
Select UTF-8 when importing the CSV, and do not modify the original.
An inaccessible folder or locked path
Narrow the scope to an accessible practice copy first.

sections.heading: What this list does and does not tell you

blocks.text: The result contains file information observed during the run. It is neither a duplicate-content check nor a backup you can restore from. Two documents with the same file size can have different contents. If you need hash comparisons, define that as a separate task and add the required columns.

This beginner example does not cover other programs changing names or contents during a scan, network-drive delays, or collecting very large numbers of files in memory. A disk-write failure can leave an incomplete outputs folder, so check both the completion message and the number of result rows.
